title: Apply sustainable farming practices to conserve the ecological environment

lessons.title: Conserving soil and veld
lessons.html:
Why sustainable practices matter

Sustainable farming means producing food and income today without damaging the soil, water, veld and wildlife that the farm will need in future. Soil that washes away takes hundreds of years to form again. Veld that is overgrazed fills with weeds and bare patches. The Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983 requires land users to protect soil, veld and water and to control declared weeds and invader plants.

Protecting the soil

  • Keep the soil covered. Leave crop residues, plant cover crops or use mulch. Bare soil is washed away by rain and blown away by wind.
  • Reduce tillage. Minimum tillage or no-till (conservation agriculture) disturbs the soil less and keeps its structure and organic matter.
  • Rotate crops. For example, rotate maize with soya beans or other legumes. Legumes add nitrogen and rotations break pest and disease cycles.
  • Work along the contour. Plough and plant across the slope, not up and down it. Keep contour banks and grassed waterways in good order.
  • Add organic matter. Compost and manure feed soil life and help soil hold water.
  • Do not work wet soil with heavy machines; it causes compaction.

Looking after the veld

  • Keep stock numbers within the grazing capacity of the veld.
  • Use camps and rotate grazing so plants can rest and recover.
  • Watch for signs of overgrazing: bare soil, loss of good grasses, more unpalatable plants, erosion gullies and paths.
  • Do not graze or burn veld in ways not in the farm's grazing plan.
  • Repair erosion early with stone packs, brush or grass before small gullies become dongas.

Example

A farmer in the Eastern Cape divides her veld into eight camps and moves the cattle every few weeks. After three seasons, more palatable grass has returned, bare patches have closed and her cattle stay in better condition through winter.

lessons.title: Protecting water, biodiversity and reducing pollution
lessons.html:
Water

  • Protect river banks and wetlands. Do not plough or plant right up to a river or into a wetland. Keep a strip of natural vegetation along streams; it filters runoff and stops banks collapsing.
  • Use irrigation water carefully. Irrigate according to crop need and soil moisture; fix leaks; prefer efficient systems such as drip.
  • Keep pollutants away from water. Store fuel, chemicals and manure away from rivers, dams and boreholes.
  • Use water legally, under the National Water Act 36 of 1998.

Biodiversity

Biodiversity means the variety of plants, animals and other living things. It supports farming with pollination, pest control and healthy soils.

  • Leave patches of natural veld, hedges and trees as habitat for birds, bees and predators of pests.
  • Do not kill owls, snakes, jackal buzzards and other predators that control rodents.
  • Remove alien invader plants such as wattle, bugweed and prickly pear. They use a lot of water and push out indigenous plants. Follow the farm's clearing plan.
  • Use wildlife-friendly methods to manage damage-causing animals, as advised by conservation authorities.

Reducing chemical pollution

  • Use Integrated Pest Management (IPM): scout first, use natural enemies and good practices, and spray only when needed.
  • Use only products registered under Act 36 of 1947 and follow the label for rate, timing and safety.
  • Never spray in windy conditions or near water.
  • Return or dispose of empty containers as the supplier or farm procedure requires. Never burn or bury them carelessly, and never reuse them for water or food.
  • Follow the fertiliser programme; extra fertiliser washes into rivers and causes algae growth.

Waste and energy

  • Compost organic waste and manure.
  • Sort and recycle plastic, metal and old drip line.
  • Switch off pumps and lights when not needed; consider solar power.

Key points

  • Keep soil covered, reduce tillage, rotate crops and work on the contour.
  • Keep stock within grazing capacity and rest the veld.
  • Protect wetlands and river banks, and use water legally and efficiently.
  • Value biodiversity and remove alien invader plants.
  • Use IPM, follow labels and keep chemicals and fertiliser out of water.
